interventions.what: Bandicam window capture of the Isle Wars Pro game window; the owner played one game from the options screen to the end screen (15:10 recording). The video file is the only output. No scripted clicks. Counters, seats and screens were read from pixels by region comparison and template matching of glyph shapes, with no OCR pass.

start_state.restore: Owner launched a new game on the unregistered Pro build from the options screen (seat 1 human, three computer seats, starting level set to the easy entry and game speed to the slow entry). Pro has no save file (C-SET-05), so no state was restored. The recording starts on the title screen; the opening deal is the first board.

args: probe: 910.37 s, 17099 video frames, variable frame rate (nominal 30), 1920x1080 H.264, AAC 48 kHz stereo, 103171810 bytes
ffmpeg 8.0.1; the panel regions were read frame by frame from the container timestamps; offsets are mm:ss.mmm video offsets
record content: the 29 turn starts, army pools, card counts and draws, the declined and the accepted human trade-in offers, and the elimination of the red seat

observations.field: reading method
observations.value: the scoreboard (top left: four rows with territory count and card count, a marker on the seat whose turn it is) read at every frame where it changed, by matching glyph shapes of its digits (no OCR); a turn starts when the marker moves to the seat; the placement message read for the army pool. Card counts at a turn start are read at the first frame of the marker, so a trade-in made a few seconds into the turn is not yet in them. The same readers as for IP1 027 and IP1 028 (E018-r0007, E018-r0011). The scoreboard's card count lags the draw screen at the end of a turn (turn 29: the draw screen showed five cards at 14:54.5 and the scoreboard still read four at 14:58).

observations.field: the first seat and the deal
observations.value: after the deal the marker flickered over the seats for about 1.7 s (00:46.4 to 00:48.2, 11 moves) and settled on the blue seat, the human, which played first (00:48.2). The deal at the options this game (starting level set to the easy entry, speed to the slow entry, at 00:20 to 00:31): counts blue/yellow/red/green 14/7/12/13 (sum 46), so the human seat held 14 countries and the three computer seats 7, 12 and 13, against 9 for the human at the middle level in the three earlier sittings (E018-r0005, r0008, r0012). First seats so far: yellow, human, red, human.

observations.field: human card draws (draw screen at the end of each capturing turn), in order
observations.value: eight draws in the eight human turns, all of which had a capture: turn 1 the five-army card (draw screen 01:20.6 with the slots empty while it is selected, the five-army card in the hand at 02:21.5), turn 5 the joker (draw screen 02:21.5 with the new card still being selected; the joker is in the hand at 03:44.6), turn 9 a strike card (the draw screen was not extracted; the hand is five, joker, strike at the scoreboard count of 3 and five, joker, strike, strike at turn 13), turn 13 a second strike card (05:13.8), turn 17 a second five-army card (07:24.6; hand five, joker, strike, strike, five), turn 21 the fifteen-army card (11:08.0; hand strike, strike, fifteen, after the trade-in took five, five and the joker), turn 25 a five-army card (12:37.4; hand strike, strike, fifteen, five), turn 29 the shield card (14:54.5; hand strike, strike, fifteen, five, shield). The fifteen-army card is seen for the first time in the four sittings (IP1 026: not seen in 45 draws), and the shield card was drawn by the human at the end of the game and held; no strike was ever played against the human.

observations.field: human trade-in offer 1, turn 17, declined (05:45.6 to 05:59.3)
observations.value: the hand held four cards: five, joker, strike, strike (count 4 at the turn start). The offer (two buttons, accept or decline, with a text asking to click three matching cards) came after income and before placement. The set strike, strike and joker was available (a strike match with a joker). The owner kept the offer open about 13 s, clicked no card (no card border in any frame), and pressed the decline button; the placement panel followed at 06:00.0 with the pool unchanged at 10 (one island named in the message, as at the turn start), and the turn went on (attacks 23 to 26, four captures; cards 5 at the next turn start). A declined offer: the first one seen in the owner's sittings (IP1 028: two offers, both accepted).

observations.field: human trade-in offer 2, turn 21, accepted (07:55.6 to 09:32.5)
observations.value: the hand held five cards: five, joker, strike, strike, five (count 5 at the turn start). The owner clicked three cards, the two five-army cards and the joker (borders on the first, second and fifth slots at 08:08.0, none at 08:00.0), left the two strike cards in the hand, kept the offer open for a further 80 s, and pressed the accept button (the offer is gone by 09:32.5); the placement pool was then 23 against 18 before (the tally screen at 07:52.0, pool 18 read at 07:54.1 and 07:55.5, and 23 read at 09:32.6 and in the panel at 09:36.0 and 09:37.0): +5 armies. Cards 5 to 2 at 09:31.1; the capture draw at the end of the turn took it to 3. Set: two five-army cards and a joker (mixed, with a joker).

observations.field: offers: complete list
observations.value: the trade-in offer appeared in exactly two human turns (17 and 21); one declined, one accepted. In turn 25 the hand held strike, strike, fifteen (no set) and in turn 29 strike, strike, fifteen, five (no set), so no offer. No strike was played by anyone in this game and no computer made a trade-in (no computer hand lost three cards at a turn start); the computer hands rose by one on capturing turns only.

observations.field: the elimination of the red seat and its cards
observations.value: the human (blue) took the red seat's last country in attack 48; at 13:57.1 red's cards went from 4 to 0 and blue's stayed 4 (the scoreboard read; blue's next draw was at the end of that turn): an eliminated seat's cards vanish and are not inherited, for a human capturer (IP1 028: a computer capturer).

observations.field: army pool against territory count, human turns
observations.value: turn (count, pool): 1 (14, 4), 5 (15, 5), 9 (15, 5): each equal to the count divided by 3 rounded down, raised to 2, with no island named; 13 (18, 10), 17 (20, 10) with 1 island named (6 and 6 plus 4 at the second turn: island amount 4), 21 (24, 18; 23 after the trade-in), 25 (29, 27), 29 (31, 25): country parts 8, 9 and 10 plus island amounts 10, 18 and 15. Computers: counts 7, 7, 3, 3, 3, 5 gave 2, 2, 5, 5, 5 and 4 (floor of 2 plus island amounts).
